questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “heed”:
questions.why: Heed = pay attention to. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “Unless you ____ the rules, you will be fined.”
questions.why: 'Unless' means 'if not', so the verb stays affirmative. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “He studied day and night lest he will fail.”
questions.why: 'Lest' takes 'should' (or the bare subjunctive), not 'will'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “I ______ for an hour when the doctor finally called me.”
questions.why: A continuing action up to a point in the past: past perfect continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “A number of patients ____ waiting outside.”
questions.why: 'A number of' takes a plural verb (unlike 'the number of'). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct conjunction: “No sooner had the bell rung ____ the students rushed out.”
questions.why: 'No sooner' is followed by 'than'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “once in a blue moon”:

opts: He spoke as if he were the owner of the house.
He spoke as if he is the owner of the house.
He spoke as if he being the owner of the house.
He spoke as if he will be the owner of the house.
questions.why: 'As if / as though' for an unreal situation takes the past subjunctive 'were'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “They expect her to complete the task soon.”
opts: She is expected to complete the task soon.
She expected to complete the task soon.
She is expected completing the task soon.
It is expected her to complete the task soon.
questions.why: Present 'expect' becomes 'is expected', infinitive kept. GPSC CBRT, May 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “She ______ have reached by now; she left two hours ago.”
questions.why: 'Should have' for an expected result. GPSC-style practice item.
